executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated two separate epidemiological updates from PAHO indicating sustained and ongoing activity in the Americas region through at least March 2026. Mpox (BSL-3 select agent) continues to circulate in the Americas with an April 2026 update, while dengue, measles, and pertussis are simultaneously elevated across the region. The convergence of multiple high-consequence pathogens alongside seasonal respiratory virus co-circulation represents a significant multi-threat burden on regional health systems.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face a complex multi-pathogen threat environment dominated by H5N1 avian influenza spillover risk, ongoing mpox transmission, and resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases alongside hyperendemic arboviral activity.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional activity
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential; zoonotic spillover risk to humans documented in Americas
Prolonged multi-month surveillance window suggests enzootic establishment rather than isolated incursion
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; ensure antiviral stockpile readiness; coordinate with agricultural authorities on poultry and wildlife monitoring; issue guidance to at-risk workers

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent; clade diversity concerns relevant to severity and transmissibility assessment
Continued surveillance reporting suggests sustained community transmission beyond initial outbreak phases
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs; monitor for clade Ib importations; ensure diagnostic capacity at regional reference laboratories; coordinate cross-border case reporting

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 signals early-season elevated activity
Americas region historically experiences hyperendemic transmission with periodic surge years
Co-circulation of multiple serotypes increases severe dengue risk in previously exposed populations
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations in high-burden urban areas; ensure clinical case management capacity for severe dengue; activate early warning systems for outbreak hotspots; communicate serotype shift risks to clinicians

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 on simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation stressing health systems
PAHO April 2026 alert marks start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 influenza season
ECDC issued five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports April-May 2026 likely tracking respiratory burden in Europe
December 2025 PAHO alert flagged Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season start alongside Southern Hemisphere season end
threats.action: Monitor ICU and hospital surge capacity; promote vaccination uptake for influenza and RSV where available; ensure antiviral treatment pathways are established; coordinate sentinel surveillance between hemispheres for strain sharing

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating renewed transmission risk in the Americas
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence linked to pandemic-era immunization gaps and growing hesitancy
Americas region previously achieved elimination status making any reintroduction a public health emergency signal
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; implement catch-up immunization campaigns targeting zero-dose and under-vaccinated children; strengthen measles case-based surveillance and laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO reports issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and potentially increasing pertussis activity
Resurgence consistent with global pattern of waning vaccine immunity and potential pathogen adaptation
Infants too young to be vaccinated remain at highest mortality risk
threats.action: Review Tdap booster coverage among adolescents and adults; ensure maternal Tdap vaccination programs are active; enhance laboratory confirmation to distinguish from other respiratory illnesses; investigate potential waning immunity signals

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating yellow fever activity in the Americas
Yellow fever is a BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality in unvaccinated individuals; select agent considerations apply
Alert timing suggests epizootic or sylvatic spillover activity preceding or accompanying human cases
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; investigate epizootic activity in non-human primates as sentinel signal; ensure yellow fever vaccine supply availability; enhance entomological surveillance in affected areas

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert February 2026 indicating active chikungunya transmission concern
Co-circulation with dengue in Aedes aegypti endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation and vector control prioritization
Alert issuance suggests case counts or geographic spread exceeding expected baseline
threats.action: Reinforce integrated arboviral surveillance to distinguish chikungunya from dengue clinically and through diagnostics; sustain vector control efforts targeting shared Aedes aegypti and Ae. albopictus vectors; alert clinicians to chronic arthralgia as post-chikungunya sequela

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been identified in active surveillance reporting. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is the highest-priority concern, with PAHO issuing updates in November 2025 and March 2026 documenting sustained activity in the Americas; H5N1 carries pandemic potential and zoonotic spillover risk requiring continuous monitoring. Mpox virus (MPXV), also BSL-3, generated an April 2026 PAHO update confirming ongoing Americas transmission; clade diversity including potential clade Ib activity warrants close genomic surveillance. Yellow fever virus, a BSL-3 pathogen, triggered a March 2026 PAHO alert suggesting sylvatic or epizootic spillover activity. All three require enhanced biosafety measures in laboratory handling and coordinated international reporting under IHR frameworks.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis potential vaccine-driven antigenic and immune-evasion adaptation noted in context of two separate alerts within three months suggesting pathogen-level changes beyond coverage gaps alone
Sustained H5N1 activity in animal reservoirs across Americas increases selective pressure and reassortment risk that could generate antiviral-resistant variants
No explicit AMR laboratory data reported in available report titles; absence of description fields limits AMR signal extraction; ECDC weekly reports likely contain AMR data not accessible in titles
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert burden on Americas health systems in early 2026 suggests post-pandemic immune debt effects manifesting across vaccine-preventable and vector-borne diseases concurrently
H5N1 generating two updates over four months in Americas indicates potential enzootic establishment rather than episodic incursion, elevating pandemic preparedness urgency
Co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in overlapping Aedes vector ranges creates diagnostic confusion and resource competition for vector control
Respiratory virus co-circulation (influenza, RSV) across both hemispheres simultaneously with back-to-back seasonal transitions compresses the window for vaccine reformulation and deployment
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports April-May 2026 suggests sustained or escalating European communicable disease burden warranting close inter-regional coordination
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert is a novel non-infectious public health signal potentially indicative of broader pharmaceutical safety surveillance gaps in the Americas
